voices: Dr. Omar — male, late 30s, friendly, confident, medium-low pitch
jobs.script: OMAR: In this module, follow a patient through a visit and see how Operations and My Care contribute at different points. Notice how their work connects.
jobs.format: MP3 44.1 kHz mono 96 kbps, −16 LUFS integrated, −1 dBTP, 300 ms head/tail
jobs.captions: WebVTT from the final audio (forced alignment), speaker names as <v Noor>/<v Dr. Omar>

voices: Dr. Omar — male, late 30s, friendly, confident, medium-low pitch
jobs.script: OMAR: A patient who has to repeat their story can lose confidence in the visit. The teams need to connect their work so the patient is guided smoothly from one stage to another. As you look at the journey, consider what a clear handoff feels like from the patient’s perspective.
jobs.format: MP3 44.1 kHz mono 96 kbps, −16 LUFS integrated, −1 dBTP, 300 ms head/tail
jobs.captions: WebVTT from the final audio (forced alignment), speaker names as <v Noor>/<v Dr. Omar>

voices: Dr. Omar — male, late 30s, friendly, confident, medium-low pitch
jobs.script: OMAR: Follow the patient from booking through follow-up. Open each stage and notice when Operations, My Care, or both are involved. The sequence helps you see how separate teams contribute to one visit.
jobs.format: MP3 44.1 kHz mono 96 kbps, −16 LUFS integrated, −1 dBTP, 300 ms head/tail
jobs.captions: WebVTT from the final audio (forced alignment), speaker names as <v Noor>/<v Dr. Omar>

voices: Dr. Omar — male, late 30s, friendly, confident, medium-low pitch
jobs.script: OMAR: Operations supports the day-to-day environment, monitors KPIs, and helps recover service when something goes wrong. As you explore these activities, consider what each one means for the patient’s experience and for colleagues working across the clinic. Some issues may need attention from another team, so be clear about the part you own and when a handoff is needed.
jobs.format: MP3 44.1 kHz mono 96 kbps, −16 LUFS integrated, −1 dBTP, 300 ms head/tail
jobs.captions: WebVTT from the final audio (forced alignment), speaker names as <v Noor>/<v Dr. Omar>

voices: Dr. Omar — male, late 30s, friendly, confident, medium-low pitch
jobs.script: OMAR: Use the chart to see how Operations is organised by role. Names can change, so the directory is the place to check current contacts. When a task needs support, identify the role involved and use the current directory rather than relying on a name you remember.
jobs.format: MP3 44.1 kHz mono 96 kbps, −16 LUFS integrated, −1 dBTP, 300 ms head/tail
jobs.captions: WebVTT from the final audio (forced alignment), speaker names as <v Noor>/<v Dr. Omar>

voices: Dr. Omar — male, late 30s, friendly, confident, medium-low pitch
jobs.script: OMAR: My Care continues the relationship beyond the visit through follow-ups, programmes, and referrals. As you open each section, consider how those activities connect with what happened during the appointment. A useful handoff gives the next colleague enough context to continue the patient’s care without asking them to start their story again. That continuity matters to the patient.
jobs.format: MP3 44.1 kHz mono 96 kbps, −16 LUFS integrated, −1 dBTP, 300 ms head/tail
jobs.captions: WebVTT from the final audio (forced alignment), speaker names as <v Noor>/<v Dr. Omar>

voices: Dr. Omar — male, late 30s, friendly, confident, medium-low pitch
jobs.script: OMAR: Explore the structure and notice how the roles fit together. The diagram can help you understand where responsibilities sit, while the current directory helps you find the right contact when people or assignments change. Use both when you need to orient yourself.
jobs.format: MP3 44.1 kHz mono 96 kbps, −16 LUFS integrated, −1 dBTP, 300 ms head/tail
jobs.captions: WebVTT from the final audio (forced alignment), speaker names as <v Noor>/<v Dr. Omar>

voices: Noor — female, early-to-mid 30s, warm, calm, clear
jobs.script: NOOR: Open each abbreviation and say what it means in your own words. Connecting the short form to its meaning can make team conversations easier to follow.
